name: Currency Pair
description: Different currency pairs exhibit vastly different volatility and trading patterns. Technical analysis might be more reliable (and thus faster) for some pairs, while fundamental analysis suits others. This is the most likely explanation for multimodal distributions as different pairs would cluster in different time ranges.

name: Market Volatility
description: High volatility often favors technical analysis (faster reaction to price swings) whereas lower volatility might lend itself better to fundamental analysis (more stable for long-term assessment). Volatility directly impacts the time taken for both analyses. High volatility could create distinct clusters representing 'fast' and 'slow' volatility regimes.

name: Time of Day
description: Trading activity fluctuates throughout the day.  Overlap between major market sessions (e.g., London & New York) generally leads to increased volatility and might favour technical analysis.  During quieter periods, fundamental analysis might be more appropriate.  Different times will lead to different processing times.

name: News Event
description: Major economic news releases (e.g., interest rate decisions, GDP figures) can significantly influence both analysis types. An impending/just-released news event will drastically affect the speed and outcome of both analysis types, and create different clusters.

name: Economic Indicator
description: The specific economic indicator being released (e.g. inflation, unemployment) could be more suited for fundamental or technical analysis. Certain indicators may cause predictable response times for fundamental analysis.

name: Data Source
description: Different data providers may have varying data quality, frequency, and latency, impacting analysis time. One provider might be quicker for fundamental data, another for technical indicators.  Different sources would naturally create different time distributions.

name: Order Book Depth
description: Shallow order books can amplify price swings, potentially making technical analysis faster, but also potentially creating errors requiring re-analysis.  Deeper books might favour a more thorough fundamental approach.

name: Trading Volume
description: High trading volume can accelerate technical analysis but might also overload systems, increasing analysis time.  Low volume might make fundamental analysis more relevant and slower.

name: Workflow Configuration (Parameters)
description: The specific parameters used *within* the technical or fundamental analysis (e.g., moving average length, fundamental ratio weights) could affect processing time. Variations in the controller’s parameter settings can cause clustering.

name: System Load
description: Overall system load (CPU, memory, network) can impact the execution time of both analyses. High load will slow everything down.

name: Data Freshness
description: The age of the data used for analysis can impact its relevance and the processing time. Stale data may require more cleaning or pre-processing.

name: Holiday/Market Closure
description: Even limited market participation can change volatility characteristics, possibly affecting the success of one analysis type over another. Especially around holidays.

name: Trader's Risk Appetite
description: Although the controller chooses the mode, the trader's implicit risk preference (if reflected in historical data) might have influenced previous choices of analysis, leading to the observed distribution.

name: Correlation between Currency Pairs
description: If currency pairs are highly correlated, the analysis time for one pair might influence the time taken for another, leading to shared clusters.

name: Underlying Asset Class
description: If the forex workflow incorporates other asset classes (commodities, indices) the distinct characteristics of these assets will affect the analysis.
